The first upper slanted line slopes downward from left to right and forms 10° with the horizontal side, so its angle of inclination is -10°. Its angle with the second upper slanted line is 14°, therefore the angle of inclination of the second slanted line from left to right is -10° + 14° = 4°, that is, 4° above the horizontal line. method.method_draft: Use signed inclinations of each zig-zag segment relative to the horizontal sides of the rectangle. From the image, read that the top and bottom rectangle sides are parallel, the first slanted segment from the top-left corner to the upper-right side makes 10° with the top side, the next segment meets it with angle 14°, the lower right kink has angle 33°, and the final segment to the bottom-left corner makes 26° with the bottom side. Treat slopes from left to right as signed angles from the horizontal: the first upper segment is -10°. Since the angle between the first and second upper segments is 14°, the second segment, viewed left-to-right from the left middle point to the upper-right point, is 14° - 10° = 4° above horizontal. The bottom segment is +26° above horizontal; since the angle between it and the middle-lower segment is 33°, the middle-lower segment, viewed left-to-right from the left middle point to the lower-right point, is 26° - 33° = -7° below horizontal. Therefore θ is the angle between a line 4° above horizontal and a line 7° below horizontal, so θ = 4° + 7° = 11°.

Inside the rectangle there is a broken line forming a zigzag shape: the slanted line from the upper-left corner to a point on the upper right and the top horizontal side are marked 10°; the slanted line from near the midpoint of the left side to the same point on the upper right and the previous slanted line are marked 14° between them; the slanted line from near the midpoint of the left side to a point on the lower right and the slanted line from the lower-left corner to that point on the lower right are marked 33° between them; the bottom slanted line starting from the lower-left corner and the bottom horizontal side are marked 26°. θ is marked between the two middle slanted lines near the midpoint of the left side.
Reasoning: Represent using the directed angle of inclination of each slanted line relative to the horizontal side. Horizontally to the right is 0°, upward is positive, and downward is negative. The first upper slanted line slopes downward from left to right and forms 10° with the horizontal side, so its angle of inclination is -10°. Its angle with the second upper slanted line is 14°, therefore the angle of inclination of the second slanted line from left to right is -10° + 14° = 4°, that is, 4° above the horizontal line. The bottom slanted line slopes upward from the lower left to the point on the lower right and forms 26° with the bottom side, so its angle of inclination is +26°. Its angle with the middle-lower slanted line is 33°, so the angle of inclination of the middle-lower slanted line from left to right is 26° - 33° = -7°, that is, 7° below the horizontal line. θ is the angle between the line with angle of inclination +4° and the line with angle of inclination -7°, therefore θ = 4° + 7° = 11°.
